summary:
Merqab (مِرقاب) is an interactive 3D museum where students aged 10-15 become space detectives investigating 11 pieces of equipment NASA left behind: 4 on the Moon and 7 on Mars. Each piece is a locked case file divided into three clues. Evidence and images are revealed gradually.

To continue the investigation, the student must complete an educational mini-game inside each piece, which tests their understanding of how the machine worked and why it was left. A progress tracker shows how many cases are solved. The museum runs in any browser and also supports VR for classrooms and institutions.

Merqab answers "Abandoned but not Forgotten" by showing that nothing was truly forgotten: every piece was a deliberate engineering decision with a story behind it. It matters because it turns space history into an investigation students must understand, not just read.
details:
What it does: Merqab is a browser-based 3D museum featuring 11 pieces of NASA equipment left on the Moon (4) and Mars (7). Students explore freely and open each piece as a locked case file divided into three clues. Evidence and images appear step by step, and the student guesses why the piece was left behind before the truth is revealed. Inside every piece is an educational mini-game that must be completed to continue the investigation; it tests real understanding, so students cannot simply click through. A progress tracker shows solved cases. The museum also works in VR for classrooms and institutions.

Benefits: Active investigation builds curiosity and critical thinking, and the mini-games confirm learning. The web version needs no download, account or special hardware.

Intended impact: To help students aged 10-15 understand that every item left on the Moon and Mars was a deliberate engineering decision, and to keep the story of these missions alive.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, 3D web graphics and WebXR for VR, hosted on Netlify. NASA imagery and 3D resources were used for accuracy. AI tools (Claude) assisted with code, story writing and planning.

Creativity: The detective format, guess-before-reveal, three-clue structure and a mini-game gate on every piece turn history into a playable mystery.

Factors considered: Age-appropriate language, Arabic/English access, performance on school devices, and historical accuracy based on NASA sources.
